issues.reason: The standing half is that the duration reading is unrecorded — `(Measure e duration <n> <unit>)` needs a magnitude and a unit that "a while" does not supply; the overstated half is calling it a defect, since the indefinite-argument rule (witness + class) and the unchanged-direct-object test (`Theme`) mandate exactly these atoms, and nothing false, ill-typed or over-asserted results.

gaps_confirmed: duration objects of light-verb "take" ("take a while", "took ages") — the `Measure … duration` form requires a magnitude and a unit, so an unquantified duration NP falls through to the ordinary indefinite-NP rule
an antecedentless demonstrative "that" standing for a situation — the no-antecedent pronoun rule names he/she/they/it only, and event anaphora presupposes an antecedent clause
new_gaps: "could" has no stated mapping: the epistemic list is might / probably / must, and nothing distinguishes epistemic "could" from the past-of-can capability sense (`Can`) or fixes whether it takes a tense atom
notes: The transitive subject staying `Agent` despite inanimacy, the mandatory class atom on `sk_thing_1`, and the bare epistemic status with no tense beside it all follow the instruction set.
